How the scores work

Deal (0–100): rent-to-price, cash flow per door, cash-on-cash and cap rate, assuming 20% down at the current 30-yr rate plus an investor premium, estimated taxes, insurance, and 8% vacancy, 8% repairs, 5% capex, 8% management (plus HOA fees where listed). Market (0–100): the municipality's median price per square foot (recent closed sales, NYSAMLS), ranked across all listings. It reflects asking prices only and says nothing about the people who live in an area. This site does not rate neighborhoods by crime, schools or demographics; for that information, consult public sources directly. Overall = 60% Deal + 40% Market; the Cash-flow style is 80/20 and the Appreciation style 25/75. Land, fractional ownership and listings without a bedroom count or price are shown but not scored. Condos and townhouses are scored like single-family homes (mobile and manufactured homes are not included on this site), with any HOA/association fee from the MLS added to monthly costs. 5+ unit buildings are scored but don't count as meeting the criteria, which are rent ≥1% of price, ≥$200/door cash flow, ≥10% cash-on-cash, ≥8% cap rate, $40k–$500k and 1–4 units. Rent estimates are HUD FY2026 Fair Market Rents for the county/metro area by bedroom count (per unit). Taxes are the MLS annual tax figure when the listing has one, otherwise an estimate from NYS ORPS full-value tax rates. All scores and projections are Paul Pezzimenti's own estimates, are not supplied by or verified by the MLS, and are applied identically to every listing.

Advertisement. Properties shown are listed by other brokerages unless noted; they are not Howard Hanna listings, and availability, price and details must be confirmed with the listing broker shown on the listing. Nothing here is an appraisal, a comparative market analysis, or financial, tax, legal or investment advice, and no return is promised. Rents are HUD Fair Market Rent figures, not market rent for the specific property; taxes marked (est.) are estimated from published tax rates, not the actual bill. Data may be outdated or inaccurate. Verify everything independently and consult your own advisors before making any decision.
